items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: I'd try to talk to Mr. Ellington, see. I'd try to say something nice (unintelligible). I used to say, "Mr. Duke"-- Ellington, you know. ... He'd say, "Call me Pop."

ctx.x: Tell me a little bit more about that?
Well, the Duke Ellington, ah society, they required his, you know, employment. See? So Pop put him in the

and -- in the employment, see? And then -- which was a show, I mean, you know, is naturally he was famous, you know? Well you never new about this industry, show business, you know. You may have to broadcast, you may have to do matinees, you know, you may have to do what they call the new marquee, which was the open air theater, like somewhere up there in the Big Apple, they called it, Central Park, West. They got some great theaters in there. You know? And it's for, I mean, what we call some say trades, you know…
